Minorite
MY-nuh-ryt
n. (a Friar Minor; a Franciscan, from the order's own title Fratres Minores)
Latin minor, lesser; the Order of Friars Minor, Ordo Fratrum Minorum, a name Francis chose so that his brothers should be the lesser and not the greater.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Minorite is the older English name for a Franciscan, taken from the order's own title: Friars Minor, the Lesser Brothers. The choice of name was deliberate and it is the best thing about the order. Francis would not have his men be maiores, the greater, the term for the ruling class of an Italian town; they were to be the lesser, ranked below. That instinct is straight out of the gospels. “whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister” (Mat 20:26); “whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted” (Luk 14:11); and the refusal of titles, “But be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Christ; and all ye are brethren” (Mat 23:8). In England the Minorites gave their name to streets and districts where their houses stood, and their early reputation was for learning as well as poverty — Grosseteste taught them, and Ockham and Bacon came out of them. The irony the name invites is that an order constituted as the lesser came to hold chairs, bishoprics and the ear of princes. Humility written into a constitution does not stay there by itself.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines minor as less, smaller, inferior; minorite as a Franciscan friar; and minister as one who serves, an agent acting under another, and in religion one who serves at the altar or preaches.

expand to see more

MINORITE, n. A Franciscan friar; one of the order of Friars Minor.

MINOR, a. Less; smaller; inferior; as the minor part of the society.

MINISTER, n. One who serves; a servant; an agent acting under the authority of another; one to whom a sovereign commits the administration of government.

MINISTER, n. One who serves at the altar; one who performs sacerdotal duties; the pastor of a church, duly authorized to preach the gospel.

HUMBLE, a. Low; opposed to high or lofty; modest; meek; submissive; having a low opinion of one's self.

Key Scripture

Mat 20:26 — "But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister;"

Luk 14:11 — "For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted."

Mat 23:8 — "But be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Christ; and all ye are brethren."

Phi 2:3 — "Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves."

Modern Corruption

The Lesser Brothers: a name chosen to put the friars below everyone, borne by an order that came to hold chairs and bishoprics.

expand to see more

The corruption is the slow reversal of a name. An order constituted as minores ended with cardinals in it, which is not a scandal peculiar to Rome but the ordinary gravity of institutions. Paul's remedy is not a title but a habit of mind: “Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves” (Phi 2:3). Lowliness that has to be codified has usually already gone.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the one Francis saw in the gospels and stated in a name: Christian greatness is service and nothing else. “whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister” (Mat 20:26) — and every church that builds a platform should read it again.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin minor, lesser; Greek diakonos (G1249), a servant; Greek tapeinophrosune (G5012), lowliness of mind; Greek adelphos (G80), brother; Hebrew anav (H6035), humble.

expand to see more

Latin minor — lesser; the whole argument of the order's name.

Greek diakonos (G1249) — a servant, one who waits on another; “let him be your minister” (Mat 20:26).

Greek tapeinophrosune (G5012) — lowliness of mind; “in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves” (Phi 2:3).

Greek adelphos (G80) — brother; “all ye are brethren” (Mat 23:8).

Hebrew anav (H6035) — humble, afflicted, meek; the word of Moses and of the Messiah.

Usage

"“But be not ye called Rabbi” (Mat 23:8) — the text behind the choice of the name."

"“he that humbleth himself shall be exalted” (Luk 14:11) — the promise, and the warning against engineering it."

"“in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves” (Phi 2:3) — lowliness as a practice, not a title."
